annotation.title_clean: On Care Robots and the Ethics of Tracking: A Transdisciplinary Ethics on Care Robots seen through a Posthuman and Performative Discussion on Tracking and Data Availability
annotation.title_en: On Care Robots and the Ethics of Tracking: A Transdisciplinary Ethics on Care Robots seen through a Posthuman and Performative Discussion on Tracking and Data Availability
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical journal article treating care robots as data-tracking technologies, using posthuman and performative ethics plus surveillance studies. It argues the key ethical issue is not robotic intent to spy but the ubiquity and availability of sensitive health data in care contexts, which invites appropriation and commodification.
key_provisions_or_claims: Tracking should be treated as an inherently ethical relation in care robots.
Main concern is data availability and robotic ubiquity, not privacy intrusion by intent.
Care contexts are especially sensitive because vulnerable people are exposed to data collection.
Health data has growing commercial value, raising risk of data appropriation.
Calls for technical transparency rather than moral judgments about robots.
